objectives: Recognize and read common short-/u/ CVC word families.
Identify onset and rime in controlled word-family patterns.
Use word-family knowledge as support without abandoning grapheme-by-grapheme decoding.
Read short-/u/ words in controlled connected text.
concepts: Words in a family share a rime.
Changing the onset creates a new word while preserving the rime.
Word-family recognition supports efficiency but must not replace decoding.

definitions.definition: A group of words sharing a common rime, such as -un or -ut.
The initial consonant or consonant cluster before the vowel in a syllable.
The vowel and following sounds in a syllable.

workedExamples: sun → s + un; change s to r → run.
hut → h + ut; change h to c → cut.
mud and bud share -ud while their onsets differ.
commonMistakes: Guessing a family word from context.
Using untaught patterns in controlled text.

basic: Sort short-/u/ CVC words by family.
conceptual: Identify onset and rime in taught words.
application: Generate a new family word by changing the onset.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why word-family recognition still requires grapheme checking.
mixedReview: Read short-/u/ families and familiar vowel families while preserving decoding accuracy.

formulaOrFactBank: Word family = shared rime + changing onset
mistakeBasedRevision: If guessing occurs, return to grapheme-by-grapheme decoding.
weakTopicRevision: Practise the specific family causing confusion, then reread controlled text.

outcomes: Learner accurately reads taught short-/u/ word families.
Learner identifies shared rimes and changing onsets.
Learner uses family patterns as support while checking every grapheme.
Learner applies short-/u/ decoding in controlled connected reading.

questions.question: Which words belong to the -un family?
Which words belong to the -ut family?
What stays the same in sun and run?
What changes when sun becomes run?
Which word can be made by changing the first sound in hut to /c/?
Which word belongs with cup and pup?
Why should a learner still sound out a word in a word family?
options: To verify every grapheme and avoid guessing

questions.question: Which pair has the same rime?
Which word does NOT belong with sun, run, and fun?
If a learner reads cut as cot, what should they check?
Which word completes the controlled sentence: “The pup is ___.”
What is the safest strategy when reading a new -ut word?
options: Decode the onset and rime, then check each grapheme

questions.question: Which set contains only short-/u/ CVC words?
Why use controlled text after word-family practice?
options: To apply accurate decoding in connected reading

questions.question: What is the main goal of this lesson?
options: Read short-/u/ word families accurately while maintaining full decoding and controlled reading
